summary.text: Ashley Bell is the Democratic nominee for North Carolina's 10th Congressional District, a physician assistant and educator who describes herself as not a career politician. A Texas native, she trained as a physician assistant at Wake Forest and has taught in public schools and at the university level. She is running on health care, education, and cost-of-living issues.

paragraphs.text: Born in Tyler, Texas, and graduated from Henderson High School; she says she was raised in rural East Texas by small-business owners and was the first in her family to attend college.

Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Houston (2003), a graduate degree from Wake Forest University School of Medicine (2011), and a graduate degree from the University of Lynchburg (2019); according to her campaign website, the latter is a Doctor of Medical Science.
According to her campaign website, she began her career as a junior high and high school band director in Texas before moving into medicine.

Works as a physician assistant; according to her campaign website, she has about 15 years of clinical experience in emergency medicine, primary care, rural clinics, and telemedicine in North Carolina.
Works as an educator; her campaign website describes about 20 years in education, including as a public school teacher and a university professor teaching physician assistant students.

Says she served on national boards and committees in her profession; Ballotpedia lists affiliations with the American Academy of Physician Associates, the Physician Assistant Education Association, the American Association of University Professors, and Democratic Women of North Carolina.
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 47.3 percent of the vote; she has not previously held elected office. According to her campaign website, she lives and works in the Triad.
